refnamediv.refpurpose: Convert string from one codepage to another

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.parameters;
in_codepage
The codepage of the subject string. Either the codepage name or identifier.
An int is a Windows codepage identifier, such as 1251 or 65001, from the table of codepages known to PHP. 0 stands for the ANSI codepage and 1 for the OEM codepage of the system. An identifier that is not in the table, such as the UTF-16 and UTF-32 codepages (1200, 1201, 12000 and 12001), throws a ValueError.
A string is always read as a codepage name, never as an identifier: "cp1251" is accepted, but "1251" is not an identifier. The name is compared, ignoring case, with the names and aliases of the same table as the input_encoding and output_encoding settings. An empty string means UTF-8. A name that is not in the table does not throw: it is treated as the ANSI codepage of the system.
out_codepage
The codepage to convert the subject string to. Either the codepage name or identifier.
An int is a Windows codepage identifier, such as 1251 or 65001, from the table of codepages known to PHP. 0 stands for the ANSI codepage and 1 for the OEM codepage of the system. An identifier that is not in the table, such as the UTF-16 and UTF-32 codepages (1200, 1201, 12000 and 12001), throws a ValueError.
A string is always read as a codepage name, never as an identifier: "cp1251" is accepted, but "1251" is not an identifier. The name is compared, ignoring case, with the names and aliases of the same table as the input_encoding and output_encoding settings. An empty string means UTF-8. A name that is not in the table does not throw: it is treated as the ANSI codepage of the system.
subject
The string to convert.
